ai.description: Daniel's Night Frog is a small, 25–30 mm frog with a brown back and cream-colored belly. It is distinguished by its pointed snout and prominent, fleshy, triangular webbing between its toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus danieli* is best distinguished by its prominent, elongated, and pointed snout, which is significantly more tapered than the rounded snouts of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Nyctibatrachus danieli* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Daniel's Night Frog is nocturnal and exhibits unique parental care, where males guard egg clutches laid on rocks near streams to protect them from predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus danieli* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 20–40 eggs on wet rocks near streams, which undergo direct development without a free-swimming stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus danieli* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Nyctibatrachus danieli* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes produced by males along rocky, fast-flowing mountain streams.
